title: RockDesk — remote desktop and remote control your AI agents can use: one ID for every machine
excerpt: RockDesk: remote desktop, terminal, file transfer, folder mounting, port forwarding and VPN in one app — and Claude Code, Codex, Trae or WorkBuddy can use it too. Peer-to-peer, end-to-end encrypted. Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS and the web.
content_html:
One ID. Every machine you own.

Remote desktop, terminal, files, port forwarding and VPN in one app — and Claude Code, Codex, Trae or WorkBuddy can work on any of your machines from a single sentence. Peer-to-peer and end-to-end encrypted.

Direct P2P

relay only when it can’t punch through

End-to-end encrypted

servers only see ciphertext

Every platform

Windows · macOS · Linux · Android · iOS · Web

Built for AI agents

Skill · CLI

Waiting is sped up (marked in the video). Device IDs in the video are placeholders.

🤖

Your AI agent can use it

Give Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Trae or WorkBuddy the RockDesk skill and it drives the rds command line on your other machines: runs commands, takes and reads screenshots, clicks and types, copies files and opens port forwards — with exactly the permissions that machine gives you.

🖥️

Remote desktop

AV1 between computers, much sharper on the same bandwidth; low-latency H.264 elsewhere, hardware-encoded where the machine can. Clipboard text and images sync both ways. On a phone: two-finger tap for right click, type with your phone’s keyboard.

📁

Terminal and files

An ssh-like terminal whose sessions survive a dropped connection; resumable copy and folder sync; mount a remote folder as a local one between Windows, macOS and Linux.

🔌

Port forwarding and VPN

Map a database or web app the other side can reach to a local port; bring up a VPN into its LAN, or send your traffic out through it.

🔒

Security you can check

Every device has its own certificate; every connection is QUIC + TLS 1.3, end to end. The machine being reached decides who gets in — key pairs (like ssh), one-time passwords, or a click on “Allow” — and what they may use. Our servers only introduce the two ends and relay ciphertext.

🌐

Direct first, relays worldwide

Hole punching first, and LAN traffic stays on the LAN. When a direct path is impossible, a relay carries it — nodes in China and the US, picked by where the two ends are.

Beyond the screen — a full remote toolkit

The rds command line does everything the app does: mount folders, run shells, forward ports / serial / USB, reach the private network — and AI agents drive it through the skill.

Directory Mount

Mount a remote folder as a local disk — edit, grep and build across machines.

Remote Terminal

Run shells and scripts headlessly — let an AI agent automate whole workflows.

Port Forwarding

Reach a service behind the remote — a DB, web app or VNC — as a local port.

Private Network

Form a LAN with the remote and reach every device on its private network.

Serial Forwarding

Use a remote serial device (/dev/ttyUSB) locally — flash and debug hardware.

USB Forwarding

Attach a USB device plugged into the remote over USB/IP, as if local (Linux).

Give your AI agent the skill

In Claude Code or a similar agent, say this once in the chat and it installs the skill itself. Then just ask: “run a task on 123456789”.

Install the skill at https://rockdesk.io/rockdesk-cli.md

The skill is one Markdown file — read it first if you like: https://rockdesk.io/rockdesk-cli.md · How AI agents use it
